A_target.statement:
Let $n = p q$ with $p \ne q$ primes, and $e d \equiv 1 \pmod {\map \phi n}$.
Then for every $m \in \Z$:
:$\paren {m^e}^d \equiv m \pmod n$
so [[Definition:RSA Algorithm|RSA]] decryption inverts encryption.

substitutions.the modulus N: n = pq, and separately p and q

object_map.reformulation: Specialize Euler's theorem to the RSA exponent, handling messages not coprime to n prime by prime.

validity_conditions: Messages divisible by p or q are not coprime to n, so the congruence is checked modulo p and q separately.
The two congruences combine by the Chinese Remainder Theorem since p and q are distinct.
proof_plan: If $m \perp n$, the source result gives $m^{e d} = m \paren {m^{\map \phi n} }^k \equiv m \pmod n$.

In general, work modulo $p$: if $p \divides m$ both sides are $0$; otherwise $m^{p - 1} \equiv 1 \pmod p$, so $m^{e d} = m \paren {m^{p - 1} }^{k \paren {q - 1} } \equiv m \pmod p$.
The same holds modulo $q$.

By the [[Chinese Remainder Theorem]], $m^{e d} \equiv m \pmod {p q}$.
{{qed}}
